title: orbitopt multi-spacecraft relative state (RelativeState v1)
description: The state of one spacecraft relative to another (E12-01, task #391): the chaser's position/velocity minus the target's, expressed at one shared epoch in one shared frame. Both vectors are SI (metres, m/s) exactly like HandoffState's position_m/velocity_m_s -- the unit is carried by the field name, and orbitopt.mission.multispacecraft.RelativeState.from_states refuses two HandoffStates whose frames differ or whose epochs disagree beyond the alignment tolerance, so a relative state is only ever formed from same-frame, same-epoch (within tolerance) states. Epochs are MJD2000 day-labels counted on the declared timescale (orbitopt.timescales convention); comparisons go through Epoch.to_tdb_seconds(). Structural rules JSON Schema can express live here; finiteness and epoch representability are checked by orbitopt.mission.multispacecraft. Compatibility policy: adding optional fields is not a breaking change; removing/renaming/narrowing is and gets relative-state-2.0.json.

target_id.description: spacecraft_id of the reference member of the pair (role TARGET in the mission).

chaser_id.description: spacecraft_id of the relative member of the pair (role CHASER). Must differ from target_id.

frame.description: The single frame both member states were expressed in when the difference was taken. Mixing frames (a GCRS r minus an ECEF r) is meaningless and is rejected at construction, not here.

metadata.description: Free-form producer annotations. Optional; readers must not depend on any particular key.

epoch.description: Mission instant: MJD2000 day-labels plus the timescale they are counted on. The timescale is mandatory -- a TT epoch is never treated as UTC.

vec3.description: Three finite numbers (finiteness enforced by orbitopt.mission.multispacecraft, matching orbitopt.mission.contract).
